elements.brief_element: The system is an offline evaluation harness that executes scenario suites against an AI system and grades the results.
elements.brief_evidence: “how our offline evaluation harness executes scenario suites against an AI system and grades the results”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstructed purpose identifies “an evaluation-harness orchestration procedure” that executes scenarios against an isolated system, grades outputs, assembles a scorecard, and compares it with a baseline.
elements.note: The domain and overall purpose are accurately recovered.

elements.brief_element: Each run starts from a pinned suite.
elements.brief_evidence: “Each run starts from a pinned suite”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The first reconstructed component is “Pinned suite,” and the “Pinned run preparation” flow begins with that component.
elements.note: The starting point and pinning concept are clear.

elements.brief_element: The pinned suite contains frozen scenario definitions.
elements.brief_evidence: “a pinned suite containing frozen scenario definitions”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “Immutable scenario versions” as being selected by the pinned suite and records the constraint that the run is pinned to immutable scenario versions.
elements.note: “Immutable scenario versions” faithfully communicates frozen definitions.

elements.brief_element: The pinned suite contains a fingerprint of the tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, and rubric versions.
elements.brief_evidence: “a fingerprint of the tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, and rubric versions”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A “Run fingerprint” component is recovered and supplied to bounded execution, but no reconstruction entry identifies its constituent tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, or rubric versions.
elements.note: The fingerprint exists, but the compatibility-defining fields inside it are omitted.

elements.brief_element: Scenario wording changes require new scenario versions rather than editing existing scenarios in place.
elements.brief_evidence: “Because wording changes invalidate historical comparisons, scenarios receive new versions instead of being edited in place.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction recovers “Immutable scenario versions” and a pinned-run constraint, but it does not state that wording changes invalidate comparisons or that a changed scenario must receive a new version.
elements.note: Immutability is communicated, but the explicit versioning rule and its comparison rationale are not.

elements.brief_element: A scheduler fans scenario work out to a bounded pool of workers.
elements.brief_evidence: “A scheduler fans work out to a bounded pool of workers”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “Bounded scheduler” sends a directed edge labeled “bounded fan-out” to the “Worker pool.”
elements.note: Scheduler ownership and bounded fan-out are explicit.

elements.brief_element: Workers target an isolated instance of the system under test.
elements.brief_evidence: “targeting an isolated instance of the system under test”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The worker pool sends “scenario steps” to a server labeled “Isolated SUT,” and the reconstruction records isolation as an execution constraint.
elements.note: The isolated execution target is directly recoverable.

elements.brief_element: Evaluation workers must never target the shared production instance.
elements.brief_evidence: “never the shared production instance”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The target is explicitly labeled “Isolated SUT,” but no reconstruction entry names the shared production instance or expresses an explicit prohibition against using it.
elements.note: Isolation strongly suggests the boundary, but the categorical production exclusion is not directly stated.

elements.brief_element: Each worker performs a scenario's steps in order.
elements.brief_evidence: “Each worker performs a scenario's steps in order”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The worker pool sends an edge labeled “scenario steps” to the isolated SUT, but no reconstruction entry states or depicts within-scenario step ordering.
elements.note: Scenario execution is shown, but ordered execution is not recoverable.

elements.brief_element: Each worker captures the full transcript.
elements.brief_evidence: “captures both the full transcript”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A component labeled “Transcript + artifact” receives a line from the worker area, but the reconstruction does not establish that the transcript is full rather than partial.
elements.note: Transcript capture is present; completeness is omitted.

elements.brief_element: Each worker captures the final artifact.
elements.brief_evidence: “and final artifact”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The worker-pool area points to “Transcript + artifact,” which then supplies the completed-scenario grading flow.
elements.note: Artifact capture and downstream use are clear, although the adjacent edge's “retry” label creates avoidable ambiguity.

elements.brief_element: Infrastructure failures trigger retries.
elements.brief_evidence: “Infrastructure failures trigger retries”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry connects “Infrastructure fault” to a retry route. The only visible “retry” discussed by the reconstruction points from the worker area into “Transcript + artifact,” and the reconstruction explicitly says it cannot determine what is retried or why.
elements.note: The required trigger-to-recovery relationship is not recoverable.

elements.brief_element: Failures caused by the tested system's behavior are recorded.
elements.brief_evidence: “failures caused by the tested system's behavior are recorded”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A worker branch labeled “behavior failure” reaches “Product regression,” but no reconstruction entry shows that the failure is written into the scenario result or another record.
elements.note: The failure category is visible, but its required recording behavior is not.

elements.brief_element: After recording a tested-system behavior failure, the worker continues.
elements.brief_evidence: “recorded before the worker continues”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry shows the worker continuing after the “Product regression” outcome or places recording before continuation.
elements.note: The non-terminal continuation semantics are absent.

elements.brief_element: Results preserve the distinction between infrastructure failures and failures caused by tested-system behavior.
elements.brief_evidence: “Results preserve that distinction”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies separate “Infrastructure fault” and “Product regression” branches, but neither branch is visibly joined to a result record that preserves the classification.
elements.note: The categories are distinguished visually, but persistence of that distinction in results is not shown.

elements.brief_element: Operational faults must not masquerade as product regressions.
elements.brief_evidence: “so operational faults cannot masquerade as product regressions”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: Separate infrastructure-fault and behavior-failure/product-regression nodes communicate two categories, but the reconstruction contains no classification guard, result schema, or downstream handling that guarantees they remain separate.
elements.note: The intended conceptual distinction survives, but the operational guarantee does not.

elements.brief_element: Completed scenarios enter grading immediately.
elements.brief_evidence: “Completed scenarios enter grading immediately.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: “Transcript + artifact” sends a route labeled “completed scenario” directly to “Globally bounded graders,” but no reconstruction evidence expresses immediacy as a timing constraint.
elements.note: Direct handoff is shown; immediate scheduling is only implied.

elements.brief_element: Independent graders score separate criteria.
elements.brief_evidence: “Independent graders score separate criteria”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies plural “Globally bounded graders” and an annotation “criterion verdicts,” but it explicitly notes that the graders' internal coordination cannot be determined.
elements.note: Multiple criterion grading is suggested, but independence and one-criterion separation are not explicit.

elements.brief_element: The independent criterion graders operate concurrently.
elements.brief_evidence: “concurrently”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry states or visibly establishes concurrent criterion grading.
elements.note: Plural graders do not by themselves communicate concurrency.

elements.brief_element: Grading is subject to a global concurrency limit.
elements.brief_evidence: “under a global concurrency limit”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The grading component is explicitly labeled “Globally bounded graders,” and the reconstruction records that graders are globally bounded.
elements.note: The global bound is clear, even though its numeric value is intentionally unspecified.

elements.brief_element: An artifact-only grader receives the artifact without the original request.
elements.brief_evidence: “an artifact-only grader receives no original request”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction recovers an “Artifact-only grader” that sends a “blind score,” but no edge explicitly shows its artifact input or excludes the original request.
elements.note: The role name communicates artifact-only grading, but the input boundary is not fully depicted.

elements.brief_element: Withholding the original request prevents the artifact-only grader from anchoring on it.
elements.brief_evidence: “and therefore avoids anchoring on it”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The artifact-only grader's output is labeled “blind score,” but the reconstruction does not identify anchoring avoidance or connect that property specifically to withholding the request.
elements.note: Blindness is communicated at a high level; the stated rationale is omitted.

elements.brief_element: Every verdict includes supporting evidence.
elements.brief_evidence: “Every verdict includes supporting evidence.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: Verdicts are labeled “Evidence-backed verdicts” and must pass through an “Evidence required” guardrail before the “valid verdicts” route reaches assembly.
elements.note: The evidence requirement is one of the clearest transmitted behaviors.

elements.brief_element: A verdict without evidence is invalid.
elements.brief_evidence: “A verdict without evidence is invalid”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “Evidence required” guardrail receives “validate evidence,” and its failure route is labeled “invalid → retry.”
elements.note: Evidence absence is operationalized as invalidity.

elements.brief_element: An invalid verdict is retried.
elements.brief_evidence: “is retried”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A dashed route labeled “invalid → retry” returns from the evidence guardrail toward “Globally bounded graders.”
elements.note: The retry loop is explicit and directed.

elements.brief_element: If the retry also fails to supply evidence, the verdict is flagged.
elements.brief_evidence: “and is flagged if the retry also fails.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A route labeled “retry fails” reaches “Flag after retry,” but the failure-path reconstruction describes the outcome as “The run is flagged after retry,” rather than unambiguously flagging the verdict.
elements.note: The second-failure flag exists, but the ownership of the flag is ambiguous and is overstated as run-level in one reconstruction entry.

elements.brief_element: An assembler merges valid verdicts into a scorecard.
elements.brief_evidence: “An assembler merges valid verdicts into a scorecard”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “valid verdicts” route enters “Merge valid verdicts,” which points to “Run scorecard.”
elements.note: Assembly inputs, operation, and output are all clear.

elements.brief_element: The assembled scorecard is compared with a chosen baseline.
elements.brief_evidence: “and compares it with a chosen baseline”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: Both “Run scorecard” and “Chosen baseline” feed the “Fingerprints match?” comparison decision.
elements.note: The two comparison inputs and compatibility gate are visible.

elements.brief_element: The comparison narrates score movements that cross a defined threshold.
elements.brief_evidence: “narrating movements that cross a defined threshold”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A “Movement threshold” configuration sends a route labeled “narrate crossings” to “Threshold movements.”
elements.note: Threshold-based movement narration is explicitly represented.

elements.brief_element: Comparison is permitted only when both runs share the same fingerprint.
elements.brief_evidence: “Comparison is permitted only when both runs share the same fingerprint.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The run scorecard and chosen baseline enter “Fingerprints match?” and only a “match” branch reaches threshold movements, but the reconstruction notes that no non-match outcome is drawn.
elements.note: The positive compatibility gate is clear; explicit rejection or termination for mismatch is absent.

elements.brief_element: The harness retains every artifact.
elements.brief_evidence: “The harness retains every artifact”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The archive “Artifacts, transcripts & verdicts” is reached only through “Threshold movements” on a “retain run” edge. Since only the fingerprint “match” branch reaches threshold movements and no mismatch branch exists, the reconstructed process does not retain every run's artifacts.
elements.note: Retention is incorrectly made dependent on successful compatible comparison rather than applying to every run.

elements.brief_element: The harness retains every transcript.
elements.brief_evidence: “transcript” in “retains every artifact, transcript, and verdict”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The retention archive names transcripts, but its only recovered incoming route comes after matched comparison and threshold movements.
elements.note: The retained data type is correct, but the universal retention boundary is contradicted by the depicted routing.

elements.brief_element: The harness retains every verdict.
elements.brief_evidence: “and verdict” in “retains every artifact, transcript, and verdict”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The archive explicitly includes verdicts, but the reconstructed retention flow is downstream of a successful fingerprint match rather than unconditional.
elements.note: The archive contents are right; the condition under which they are retained is wrong.

elements.brief_element: Retention permits disputed scores to be re-examined.
elements.brief_evidence: “so disputed scores can be re-examined”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry identifies dispute handling or re-examination of scores from retained evidence.
elements.note: The archive is present, but its audit and dispute-resolution purpose is omitted.

elements.brief_element: Promoting a run makes that run the baseline.
elements.brief_evidence: “promoting a run makes it the baseline”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: “Promote run” sends an edge labeled “promote” to “Future baseline.”
elements.note: Promotion clearly changes the run's role to a baseline.

elements.brief_element: A promoted run becomes the baseline for future compatible runs.
elements.brief_evidence: “for future compatible runs”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The promotion target is labeled “Future baseline,” and a separate fingerprint-match gate defines compatible comparison, but no visible feedback path connects the future baseline to subsequent compatible runs.
elements.note: Future-baseline status is clear; its reuse by later compatible runs is not explicitly connected.

elements.brief_element: The primary end-to-end flow is a pinned run moving through bounded execution, evidence-backed grading, compatible baseline comparison, retention, and optional promotion.
elements.brief_evidence: “The diagram should make clear how a pinned run moves from bounded execution through evidence-backed grading and compatible baseline comparison” together with the preceding retention and promotion requirements.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction recovers an ordered path from “Pinned suite” through “Bounded scheduler,” “Worker pool,” “Transcript + artifact,” “Globally bounded graders,” evidence validation, “Merge valid verdicts,” “Run scorecard,” fingerprint comparison, retention, and “Future baseline.” However, the worker-to-artifact edge is ambiguously labeled “retry,” and retention is routed only after matched comparison.
elements.note: The overall architecture is recognizable end to end, but two important transitions are not implementation-safe.

elements.brief_element: The operational story must keep infrastructure failures distinct from product regressions throughout execution and results.
elements.brief_evidence: “while keeping infrastructure failures distinct from product regressions”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: Distinct “Infrastructure fault” and “Product regression” branches are recovered, but infrastructure retry, behavior-failure recording and continuation, and persistence of the distinction in results are absent.
elements.note: The categories are visually separated, but the required differentiated handling is incomplete.

unsupported_claims.claim: The run fingerprint is derived after the immutable scenario versions.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The “Run fingerprint” responsibility says it is “derived after the immutable scenario versions,” and the pinned-run flow orders “Immutable scenario versions” before “Run fingerprint.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief says the pinned suite contains both frozen scenarios and a fingerprint. It does not state that the fingerprint is derived from or temporally produced after the scenario versions.

unsupported_claims.claim: The worker-to-transcript-and-artifact route is a retry flow.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstructed “Execution artifact to grading” flow lists “Worker pool, retry, Transcript + artifact,” while the uncertainty list notes that the line is labeled “retry.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief says workers capture transcripts and artifacts, while infrastructure failures trigger retries. It does not support treating normal artifact capture as the retry route, and the reconstruction cannot identify a retry trigger for this edge.

unsupported_claims.claim: A tested-system behavior failure necessarily has the terminal or categorical outcome “Product regression.”
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The failure path routes “behavior failure” to a lightning node labeled “Product regression” and calls that the outcome.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires behavior failures to be recorded and kept distinct from infrastructure faults; it does not state that each individual behavior failure is conclusively a product regression or terminal outcome.

unsupported_claims.claim: The entire run, rather than the invalid verdict, is flagged when the evidence retry fails.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The retry-failure path gives the outcome “The run is flagged after retry.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief grammatically and operationally applies invalidation, retry, and subsequent flagging to the verdict, not to the whole run.

unsupported_claims.claim: Promotion occurs only after retained materials are reviewed by a human.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The constraints state, “Promotion occurs only after retained materials are reviewed by a human,” based on an archive-to-human “review” edge.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief states that promoting a run makes it the baseline, but it does not require human review or make retained-material review a precondition for promotion.

verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The evidence-backed grading path is transmitted most strongly: completed scenarios reach globally bounded graders, verdicts must include evidence, invalid verdicts loop to retry, a second failure is flagged, and only valid verdicts proceed to scorecard assembly.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: Failure handling and retention semantics are not faithfully recoverable. Infrastructure faults have no trigger-to-retry route, behavior failures are not shown as recorded before continuation, and retention of every artifact, transcript, and verdict is contradicted by routing the archive only after a successful compatible comparison.
verdict.overall_summary: The reconstruction clearly communicates the evaluation domain, major components, bounded execution, isolated SUT, evidence validation, scorecard assembly, fingerprint-gated comparison, threshold narration, and promotion. The primary architecture is recognizable, but it is not safe as an implementation plan: ordered scenario execution and concurrent independent criterion grading are under-specified; the fingerprint contents are omitted; the execution retry semantics are ambiguous; infrastructure and product failures lack their required differentiated recovery behavior; and universal retention is depicted as conditional on successful comparison. Because the board contradicts a system-defining retention boundary and leaves a critical failure/recovery path unrecoverable, the score is capped at 5.
